### Problem: Out of boundary paths {#sec-gd-p3-out}

::: {.p-statement}
A ball starts at `(startRow, startColumn)` on an $m \times n$ grid. Each move steps to an adjacent cell, and a step that crosses the border removes the ball. Count the move sequences of length at most `maxMove` that take the ball out, modulo $10^9+7$. Here $m, n \le 50$ and `maxMove` $\le 50$.

Source: [LC 576 · Out of Boundary Paths](https://leetcode.com/problems/out-of-boundary-paths/){.solved difficulty="Medium"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Right then left returns to the start, so a table indexed only by the cell has no fill order and the count of walks is infinite. The move budget is what grows. After $t$ moves the ball is at one cell, still inside, or it has already left. Leaving is the event you add; staying is the mass you push into the next layer.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[t][r][c]$ = sequences of length $t$ that are still inside and end at $(r, c)$. The backward view is $f(r, c, k)$ = ways to leave from $(r, c)$ with at most $k$ moves left.
- **Transition.** From $(r, c)$, each of the four steps either adds $dp[t][r][c]$ to the answer (the step left the grid) or adds it into $dp[t{+}1][r'][c']$.
- **Base.** $dp[0][\mathrm{start}] = 1$. Inside with no moves left is $0$. Already outside is $1$. **Answer.** The sum of every exit found while pushing layers $0, \ldots, \mathrm{maxMove}-1$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
`go(r, c, left)` returns $1$ when $(r, c)$ is already outside and $0$ when it is inside with no moves left. Otherwise it adds the four neighbours at `left - 1`. The tree has up to $4^{\mathrm{maxMove}}$ leaves. Keep this form for `maxMove` $\le 8$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("out", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def boundary_rec(m, n, max_move, start_row, start_col):
    def go(r, c, left):
        if r < 0 or r >= m or c < 0 or c >= n:
            return 1
        if left == 0:
            return 0
        return (go(r - 1, c, left - 1) + go(r + 1, c, left - 1)
                + go(r, c - 1, left - 1) + go(r, c + 1, left - 1)) % MOD
    return go(start_row, start_col, max_move)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int boundaryRec(int m, int n, int r, int c, int left) {
    const int MOD = 1000000007;
    if (r < 0 || r >= m || c < 0 || c >= n) return 1;
    if (left == 0) return 0;
    long long s = 0;
    const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
        s += boundaryRec(m, n, r + dr[k], c + dc[k], left - 1);
    return (int)(s % MOD);
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
`go(r, c, left)` depends on all three arguments. Store the first answer under that triple. A key of $(r, c)$ alone cannot: one move from $(0, 0)$ on the $2\times 2$ is $2$, and two moves is $6$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("out", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def boundary_memo(m, n, max_move, start_row, start_col):
    memo = [[[-1] * n for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(max_move + 1)]

    def go(r, c, left):
        if r < 0 or r >= m or c < 0 or c >= n:
            return 1
        if left == 0:
            return 0
        if memo[left][r][c] >= 0:
            return memo[left][r][c]
        res = (go(r - 1, c, left - 1) + go(r + 1, c, left - 1)
               + go(r, c - 1, left - 1) + go(r, c + 1, left - 1)) % MOD
        memo[left][r][c] = res
        return res

    return go(start_row, start_col, max_move)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int boundaryMemo(int m, int n, int r, int c, int left, vector<vector<vector<int>>>& memo) {
    const int MOD = 1000000007;
    if (r < 0 || r >= m || c < 0 || c >= n) return 1;
    if (left == 0) return 0;
    int& res = memo[left][r][c];
    if (res >= 0) return res;
    long long s = 0;
    const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
        s += boundaryMemo(m, n, r + dr[k], c + dc[k], left - 1, memo);
    return res = (int)(s % MOD);
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Forward layers. Start with one ball at the start in layer $0$. Push each layer into the next: an outside neighbour adds to the answer, an inside neighbour adds to layer $t + 1$. Stop before layer `maxMove`. Pushing that layer as well counts walks of length `maxMove + 1`, and sample 1 becomes $14$.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("out", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def boundary_tab(m, n, max_move, start_row, start_col):
    dp = [[[0] * n for _ in range(m)] for _ in range(max_move + 1)]
    dp[0][start_row][start_col] = 1
    out = 0
    dirs = ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1))
    for t in range(max_move):
        for r in range(m):
            for c in range(n):
                ways = dp[t][r][c]
                if ways == 0:
                    continue
                for dr, dc in dirs:
                    nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                    if nr < 0 or nr >= m or nc < 0 or nc >= n:
                        out = (out + ways) % MOD
                    else:
                        dp[t + 1][nr][nc] = (dp[t + 1][nr][nc] + ways) % MOD
    return out
```

##### C++

```cpp
int boundaryTable(int m, int n, int maxMove, int sr, int sc) {
    const int MOD = 1000000007;
    const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    vector<vector<vector<long long>>> dp(maxMove + 1, vector<vector<long long>>(m, vector<long long>(n)));
    dp[0][sr][sc] = 1;
    long long out = 0;
    for (int t = 0; t < maxMove; ++t)
        for (int r = 0; r < m; ++r)
            for (int c = 0; c < n; ++c) {
                long long ways = dp[t][r][c];
                if (ways == 0) continue;
                for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k) {
                    int nr = r + dr[k], nc = c + dc[k];
                    if (nr < 0 || nr >= m || nc < 0 || nc >= n) out = (out + ways) % MOD;
                    else dp[t + 1][nr][nc] = (dp[t + 1][nr][nc] + ways) % MOD;
                }
            }
    return (int)out;
}
```
:::

#### Rolling layers

::: {.form-next}
Layer $t + 1$ reads only layer $t$, and the cells inside one layer do not read each other. Keep `cur` and `nxt`. Writing the push back into `cur` lets one ball take several steps in a single round.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("out", "roll")
    assert str(final) == "6"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
def boundary_roll(m, n, max_move, start_row, start_col):
    cur = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
    cur[start_row][start_col] = 1
    out = 0
    dirs = ((-1, 0), (1, 0), (0, -1), (0, 1))
    for _t in range(max_move):
        nxt = [[0] * n for _ in range(m)]
        for r in range(m):
            for c in range(n):
                if cur[r][c] == 0:
                    continue
                for dr, dc in dirs:
                    nr, nc = r + dr, c + dc
                    if nr < 0 or nr >= m or nc < 0 or nc >= n:
                        out = (out + cur[r][c]) % MOD
                    else:
                        nxt[nr][nc] = (nxt[nr][nc] + cur[r][c]) % MOD
        cur = nxt
    return out

def _boundary_cell_only(m, n, max_move, sr, sc):
    memo = [[None] * n for _ in range(m)]

    def go(r, c, left):
        if r < 0 or r >= m or c < 0 or c >= n:
            return 1
        if left == 0:
            return 0
        if memo[r][c] is not None:
            return memo[r][c]
        res = (go(r - 1, c, left - 1) + go(r + 1, c, left - 1)
               + go(r, c - 1, left - 1) + go(r, c + 1, left - 1)) % MOD
        memo[r][c] = res
        return res

    return go(sr, sc, max_move)

assert boundary_roll(2, 2, 2, 0, 0) == 6
assert boundary_roll(1, 3, 3, 0, 1) == 12
assert boundary_roll(1, 1, 0, 0, 0) == 0 and boundary_roll(1, 1, 1, 0, 0) == 4
assert boundary_roll(3, 3, 1, 1, 1) == 0 and boundary_roll(3, 3, 2, 1, 1) == 4
assert boundary_roll(2, 3, 4, 0, 1) == 44
assert boundary_roll(1, 1, 50, 0, 0) == 4
assert boundary_tab(8, 50, 23, 5, 26) == boundary_roll(8, 50, 23, 5, 26) == 914783380
assert boundary_tab(2, 2, 50, 0, 0) == boundary_roll(2, 2, 50, 0, 0)
assert _boundary_cell_only(2, 2, 1, 0, 0) == 2
assert _boundary_cell_only(2, 2, 2, 0, 0) != 6 or _boundary_cell_only(2, 2, 1, 0, 0) == 2
# A shared (r, c) memo answers whichever budget was stored first.
_shared = [[None] * 2 for _ in range(2)]

def _go_shared(r, c, left, m=2, n=2):
    if r < 0 or r >= m or c < 0 or c >= n:
        return 1
    if left == 0:
        return 0
    if _shared[r][c] is not None:
        return _shared[r][c]
    res = (_go_shared(r - 1, c, left - 1) + _go_shared(r + 1, c, left - 1)
           + _go_shared(r, c - 1, left - 1) + _go_shared(r, c + 1, left - 1)) % MOD
    _shared[r][c] = res
    return res

assert _go_shared(0, 0, 1) == 2 and _go_shared(0, 0, 2) == 2
for args in ((2, 2, 2, 0, 0), (1, 3, 3, 0, 1), (1, 1, 1, 0, 0), (3, 3, 2, 1, 1), (2, 3, 4, 0, 1)):
    assert boundary_rec(*args) == boundary_memo(*args) == boundary_tab(*args) == boundary_roll(*args)
```

##### C++

```cpp
int boundaryRoll(int m, int n, int maxMove, int sr, int sc) {
    const int MOD = 1000000007;
    const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0}, dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
    vector<vector<long long>> cur(m, vector<long long>(n)), nxt;
    cur[sr][sc] = 1;
    long long out = 0;
    for (int t = 0; t < maxMove; ++t) {
        nxt.assign(m, vector<long long>(n));
        for (int r = 0; r < m; ++r)
            for (int c = 0; c < n; ++c) {
                if (cur[r][c] == 0) continue;
                for (int k = 0; k < 4; ++k) {
                    int nr = r + dr[k], nc = c + dc[k];
                    if (nr < 0 || nr >= m || nc < 0 || nc >= n) out = (out + cur[r][c]) % MOD;
                    else nxt[nr][nc] = (nxt[nr][nc] + cur[r][c]) % MOD;
                }
            }
        swap(cur, nxt);
    }
    return (int)out;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** is $O(4^{K})$. **Memo** is $O(Kmn)$ time and memory, plus $O(K)$ stack. The **table** is the same time and memory. **Rolling layers** are $O(Kmn)$ time and $O(mn)$ memory. Four partial counts each below $10^9+7$ sum past $2^{31}$; add them in a 64-bit integer and reduce once.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- `(1, 1, 0, 0, 0)` is $0$: no move is allowed, and the ball is still inside.
- `(1, 1, 1, 0, 0)` is $4$: every side is open, and a second move never happens because the ball has left.
- `(3, 3, 1, 1, 1)` is $0$: one move from the centre only reaches the middle of an edge. `(3, 3, 2, 1, 1)` is $4$.
- `(1, 3, 3, 0, 1)` is $12$: $2$ exits on move 1, $6$ on move 2, $4$ on move 3.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Memo keyed only on $(r, c)$. One move from $(0, 0)$ on the $2\times 2$ is $2$; two moves is $6$. Whichever value is stored first is what every later budget receives. The key is $(left, r, c)$.
- Updating one array in place. A ball pushed to a neighbour is pushed again, and possibly out, in the same round. Sample 2 then misses $12$. Read `cur`, write `nxt`.
- Pushing layer $K$ as well as layers $0..K-1$. Sample 1 becomes $6 + 8 = 14$.
- Adding four `int` values and reducing afterwards. The sum overflows a 32-bit integer before the modulus.
:::

**Variants.** [LC 1269 · Number of Ways to Stay in the Same Place After Some Steps](https://leetcode.com/problems/number-of-ways-to-stay-in-the-same-place-after-some-steps/){difficulty="Hard"} is the same layers on a line, and the walk must end at index $0$. [LC 688 · Knight Probability in Chessboard](https://leetcode.com/problems/knight-probability-in-chessboard/){difficulty="Medium"} pushes probability $1/8$ and sums the mass still on the board. [LC 935 · Knight Dialer](https://leetcode.com/problems/knight-dialer/){difficulty="Medium"} counts walks on the keypad graph. [LC 1575 · Count All Possible Routes](https://leetcode.com/problems/count-all-possible-routes/){difficulty="Hard"} uses remaining fuel as the layer, and a drive can skip several units of fuel. [CF 1517D · Explorer Space](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1517/D){rating="1800"} wants a closed walk of length $k$; odd $k$ is impossible on a grid, and even $k$ is twice the cheapest walk of length $k/2$.
